Visibility is a synchronous function of initial/scanner/dock position, rolls mutate state synchronously, and full drags perform adjacent-cell rolls.
Settlement is timer-driven after WEIGH LOT and disables the task controls while it runs.
The table-turn, rail/grid, token-position, collision, and die-roll changes are CSS animations/transitions rather than outcome-state evolution.
The grader replays visibility and roll state from events and checks settlement after the action transcript; event timestamps do not drive the replay.
The verifier delegates the submitted UI transcript to the independent replay grader.

configuration_reports.label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 5 has four independently oriented dice, scanner-only top-face visibility after the initial reveal, and a target sum from 10 through 20; housing cells show SEALED and scanner/dock cells reveal the top face.
Simplified mode selects a die with a labelled DIE CLAMP button (also keyboard 1-4 or rail-token selection) and rolls with the N/E/S/W pad or WASD/arrow jog keys; table rotation is optional.
ROTATE VIEW (180 degrees, optional), RESET TABLE (or R), and WEIGH LOT are available outside settlement.
autonomous_processes: After a roll, the die-token position/grid transitions and the 260 ms die-roll animation continue without a new action; the success-relevant position and orientation were already changed synchronously by the roll.
After an invalid roll, a 340 ms collision animation and readout cleanup continue without input; no logical outcome state changes.
After ROTATE VIEW, a 420 ms table-turn animation continues; the view counter changes synchronously and does not change die outcomes.

After WEIGH LOT with all dice ready, a 90 ms first settlement timer, 115 ms inter-sample timers, and a 150 ms completion timer update the visible balance waveform and then post the result; all roll, selection, rotation, reset, and weigh controls are disabled while settling.
The asynchronous result response shows a verdict or renders a fresh challenge after submission; it is post-submission result/retry handling.
grouped_control_modes: D_simplified_roll: every die-clamp selection followed by a roll-pad or keyboard jog roll across dice, seeds, and route occurrences.
D_weigh_gate: the visible pre-WEIGH LOT decision after all dice are docked.
D_view: optional 180-degree table rotation.
D_reset: RESET TABLE or R.

clause_i.reason: An observation-free policy q cannot be optimal across the generated histories: the generator randomizes four dice' initial orientations and route plans and derives a coupled target from their selected final tops, while target and scanner/face evidence are absent from I_t. The same prior selection and jog sequence can therefore require different next actions.

clause_ii.reason: At the nonempty pre-weigh gate, all four docked faces, the coupled target, rail/dock state, and available controls are visible in a bounded current screenshot, so a static visual policy can choose the next submit or recovery action. Scanner occlusion changes what is visible, but does not create a changing opportunity.

clause_iii.reason: Accepted position, orientation, and dock state change synchronously inside rollSelected when the pad or key action is delivered; leaving a scanner immediately changes visibility as part of that same action, not autonomously during a delay. The subsequent CSS motion is presentation-only. Post-WEIGH LOT settlement disables all outcome-affecting controls, so no Delta produces a strict loss of an available action.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: No qualifying common process exists: scanner/housing visibility is a synchronous consequence of the roll, roll/turn/collision animations are visual effects, and the balance waveform begins only after WEIGH LOT with controls locked.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails clause iii, so the pre-run override is not applicable. There is no autonomous outcome phase before the roll actions; settlement starts only after the administrative weigh action.
